text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
"Can a man be of use to God? Can even the wisest be of profit to him?
Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous? Does he gain anything if your ways are blameless?
Is it for your reverence that he rebukes you and brings you to judgment?
Is not your wickedness great, and your sins beyond counting?
For you took pledges from your brothers without cause and stripped the naked of their clothing.

versions.text: For you took your neighbor's pledge for nothing and stripped the naked of their clothing.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has the plural 'your brothers' (אַחֶיךָ), and 'חִנָּם' means 'without cause / for no reason,' not 'for nothing' — which in English can be misread as 'you gained nothing by it.'

text: You gave no water to the weary and withheld bread from the hungry.
The land belonged to the man of power, and the favored one lived on it.
You sent widows away empty-handed and crushed the strength of orphans.
That is why snares surround you and sudden terror overwhelms you,
why darkness blinds you and a flood of water covers you over.
Is not God in the heights of heaven? Look how high the loftiest stars are!
Yet you say, 'What does God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?

versions.text: Yet you say, "What does God know? Can he judge through such darkness?
versions.explanation: This is a quotation inside Eliphaz's speech, which itself opened with double quotation marks in verse 2. Nested speech should use single quotation marks for consistency and clarity when read aloud.

versions.text: Yet you say, 'What does God know? Can he judge through such darkness?
versions.explanation: עֲרָפֶל denotes dense, gloomy cloud-darkness; 'the thick darkness' preserves that image and links directly to the 'thick clouds' of the next verse, whereas 'such darkness' is a vaguer paraphrase with an added demonstrative not in the Hebrew.

text: Thick clouds veil him, so he cannot see, as he walks the vault of heaven.'

versions.text: Thick clouds veil him, so he cannot see, as he walks the vault of heaven."
versions.explanation: Closing mark must match the nested quotation opened in verse 13; use a single closing quotation mark for the quoted words of Job inside Eliphaz's speech.

text: Will you keep to the ancient path that wicked men have trodden?
They were snatched away before their time, their foundations washed out by a flood.
They said to God, "Leave us alone! What can the Almighty do to us?"
Yet it was he who filled their houses with good things. So the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
The righteous see their ruin and rejoice; the innocent mock them:
"Surely our adversaries are wiped out, and fire has devoured what they left behind."
Come to terms with God and be at peace with him; then good will come to you.
Receive instruction from his mouth and store up his words in your heart.
If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored; put wrongdoing far from your tent,
and lay your gold in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the stones of the streambeds.

versions.text: and throw your gold in the dust, your gold of Ophir among the stones of the streambeds.
versions.explanation: The repetition of 'your gold ... your gold' is awkward for oral reading; the second line simply names 'Ophir' as the gold's origin. 'Lay' also reflects the verb שִׁית ('place, set') more closely than 'throw.'

text: Then the Almighty himself will be your gold, your treasure of silver.
Then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
You will pray to him, and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
What you decide will be done, and light will shine on your ways.
When others are brought low, you will say, "Lift them up!" and he will save the downcast.
He will deliver even the guilty; by the cleanness of your hands he will be set free.

versions.text: He will deliver even the guilty; through the cleanness of your hands they will be delivered.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew subject is singular throughout ('the one who is not innocent ... he will be delivered'); the shift to 'they' breaks the agreement. Also avoids repeating 'deliver ... delivered' in the same line.
